newsitem.title: UK: Premier Oil buys Indonesia oil and gas stake.
newsitem.headline: Premier Oil buys Indonesia oil and gas stake.

text.p: UK-based Premier Oil said on Friday it had completed negotiations to buy Sumatra Gulf Oil Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Chevron International Ltd, for $72 million.

Sumatra, whose sole asset is a 66.67 percent stake in the Natuna Sea Block 'A' Production Sharing Contract, off Indonesia's shores, which includes the currently-producing Anoa oilfield and considerable gas reserves, is a production sharing contractor to Pertamina, the Indonesian state-owned oil company.
Premier said in a statement it would fund the acquisition from existing facilities and would act as operator.
"A phased transition process has been agreed with Chevron and Pertamina that allows for effective transfer of people and skills from the current operator," Premier said.
Premier estimates that total remaining recoverable reserves in the Anoa oilfield are 9.7 million barrels. The oilfield is presently producing 13,000 barrels per day.
Anoa oil is one of the highest value Indonesian crudes, trading at a premium to Brent, Premier said. It expects to cut costs to boost efficiency and profits "in the near future".
The block also contains considerable quantities of high quality gas -- 1081 btu per million cubic feet.

Gross proven and probable reserves have been estimated by Premier to be 650 billion cubic feet in the Anoa field and possible reserves on the block to be 1.5 trillion cubic feet, including two recent discoveries.

Premier, which said the acquistion was a "real coup", is mulling how best to develop the gas with targeted first production before the year 2000. The company said it had identified oil exploration and appraisal opportunities with prospect sizes ranging up to 150 million barrels of oil.
Premier already holds a stakes in Venezuela's Pangkah and Halmahera blocks.

"This acquisition in the Natuna 'A' PSC is a real coup for Premier which builds on our Far East business, establishing ourselves in Indonesia as a production operator and developing a near term gas business in the region," said Charles Jamieson, Premier's chief executive.
